You are assessing claims to advise a decision in a fictional case. Use only the supplied case material. The task is to determine what the records establish about each candidate claim, then give a brief decision note.

For each claim, return status, confidence, and citations. Status is "supported" if the available records establish the claim, "contradicted" if they establish its negation, or "unresolved" if they do neither. Confidence is your integer estimate from 0 to 100 of whether the claim itself is true, not your confidence in the status label. Limited evidence can inform that number without establishing the claim. Cite exact source IDs for evidence that establishes the claim or its negation. Use an empty list if no decisive source ID is available. Do not invent identifiers. A handoff may summarize record material. A follow-up is a new source when present. In your note, briefly distinguish decisive evidence from provisional indications.

{"scenario":"Brook Post subscriptions","question":"Can the incident lead close a postal service ticket?","claims":{"A":"The ticket intake had zero original delivery complaints.","B":"The print room released 140 replacement issues on Monday.","C":"All 140 replacement issues were delivered on Tuesday."},"handoff":"The case concerns whether the incident lead can close a postal service ticket related to Brook Post subscriptions. The prior assessment found Claim A—that there were zero original delivery complaints—contradicted by source S3, which records 37 complaints before replacements. Claim B, that 140 replacement issues were released Monday, is supported by the printer dispatch manifest (S1). Claim C, that all 140 replacements were delivered Tuesday, remains unresolved; while the coordinator marks delivery complete when the van departs and expects delivery Tuesday (S2), there is no confirmation all replacements arrived. Since full delivery completion is unconfirmed and original complaints exist, the incident lead likely should not close the ticket yet.","follow_up":{}}

Claim B is decisively supported by the printer dispatch manifest in S1 showing 140 replacements released Monday. Claim C remains unresolved because while S2 indicates the coordinator marked delivery complete upon van departure and expected delivery Tuesday, there is no direct confirmation that all 140 replacements were actually delivered. Given the presence of original complaints and unconfirmed full delivery, the incident lead should not close the postal service ticket yet."}

parsed.note: Claim A is decisively contradicted by source S3, which documents 37 original delivery complaints. Claim B is decisively supported by the printer dispatch manifest in S1 showing 140 replacements released Monday. Claim C remains unresolved because while S2 indicates the coordinator marked delivery complete upon van departure and expected delivery Tuesday, there is no direct confirmation that all 140 replacements were actually delivered. Given the presence of original complaints and unconfirmed full delivery, the incident lead should not close the postal service ticket yet.
